subject: Cold-start embedding seed plan + rerank sanity checks for Acme catalog
messages:
From: Julia Ross <julia.ross@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cold start strategy for product embeddings (catalog ~3M items)

Hi Rachel —

We're ramping up the embeddings + rerank work for our product catalog (roughly 3M SKU-level records). Before we kick off the Dedicated onboarding, the engineering team asked for a concrete cold-start seeding approach and a short rerank sanity checklist so we can validate quality before committing to a full backfill.

Key constraints:
- We need the initial public catalog search to be available within 3 weeks (read-only search okay for the first week).
- We currently have Pinecone for vector storage but are open to alternatives if cost/ops improve.
- We want a quick metric check: baseline NDCG@10 and a small human-labeled set for sanity.

Can you send a proposed phased plan, who from Redwood will own which tasks, and any pre-built artifacts (templates / scripts) we can reuse? Attaching a small sample export of our catalog (acme_seed_sample.csv) to help.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Ross
Head of Search, Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Cold start strategy for product embeddings (catalog ~3M items)

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the sample, that helps a lot. High-level proposal (short timeline version) below — I attached a seed_plan_v1.xlsx and a rerank_eval_template.csv so your team can see the specific checks we recommend.

Phase 0 — Discovery (2 business days)
- Deliverable: final scope doc + shard/ID mapping (owner: Acme eng, reviewed by Naomi)
- Inputs we need: primary SKU id, canonical description field, category taxonomy, and any existing sparse signals (clicks, ctr).

Phase 1 — Cold Seed (3–5 business days)
- Goal: push a first set of vectors for a deterministic subset (seed = 50k high-impact SKUs) so frontend and ranking can validate end-to-end.
- Owner: Redwood (Karthik leads ingestion + quantization profile) + Acme (validation)
- Steps: export seed CSV -> local embedding generation (can run on your infra or ours) -> push to vector store (we support Pinecone, Milvus, RedisVector)
- Acceptance: search latency <= target (we'll define SLO) and quick smoke-check on top-10 results for 20 queries.

Phase 2 — Rerank sanity & baseline (5 business days)
- Goal: run rerank A/B on seed set and measure quality delta vs sparse baseline
- Steps: use rerank_eval_template.csv for human labels (we recommend 200 queries, 3 labels each), compute NDCG@10 / MRR / recall@k
- Owner: Redwood (Marissa supports eval harness), Acme (labeling & review)

Phase 3 — Incremental backfill + monitoring (2–4 weeks)
- Goal: full catalog backfill with throttled ingestion, warm KV caches, and post-backfill QA
- Steps: chunked backfill, incremental replay of recent interactions, schedule rerank regression checks, enable caching & batching config suggested by Redwood Optimize

Risks & mitigations:
- Vector store cost: Karthik will provide a sizing estimate and cheaper config (16-bit quant) options.
- Cold-cache latency spike: plan a staged rollout and warm commonly-accessed prefixes first.
- Model regressions: we will run rerank evals after each major backfill step and block rollout on regressions > 3% NDCG drop.

Next actions I propose this week:
1) Quick call to align owners and finalize scope (30 min) — I'll send an invite.
2) Share your labeling resource ETA so we can populate rerank_eval_template.csv.
3) Karthik will send a vector-store sizing estimate and recommended config.

Attachments: seed_plan_v1.xlsx (detailed task list), rerank_eval_template.csv (label template)

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Quick notes on infra and sizing we should include in the plan:

1) Vector DB & storage config
- For 3M vectors, with 1536-d float32 that's ~18GB raw; with 8-bit/4-bit or 16-bit quanting we can drop to ~4–8GB. Recommend starting with a quantized profile in Redwood Dedicated to minimize transfer/time.
- We'll provide two ingestion modes: bulk push (for backfill) and streaming (for near-real-time updates).

2) Backfill chunking strategy
- Use chunk sizes that keep ingestion p95 under the vector-store's rate limits. We'll run a short pre-flight to pick chunk size (suggest 20k per job).

3) KV cache warmup
- Prioritize warmup keys for top categories and recent 30-day hot SKUs. We should capture a small replay trace (we can help capture) to pre-populate caches.

I'll attach a brief sizing table in the seed_plan_v1.xlsx and will flag recommended instance counts for the Dedicated pool.

—Karthik
